fig1_faraday_emf.svg: A loop in a uniform field B(t) = B0 sin(wt): the flux Phi(t) (blue, via the module's surface integral) and the induced EMF = -dPhi/dt (orange). The EMF leads the flux by 90 degrees and always opposes the change in flux (Lenz's law); here the rising-flux quarter has sign -1.
fig2_inductor_energy.svg: Energy stored in a 1000-turn solenoid vs current. The circuit formula W = (1/2) L I^2 (curve) and the magnetic-field integral (1/2mu0) integral B^2 dV (dots) coincide -- the same energy whether attributed to the inductor or to the field.
